markdown: --- Page source: [page 1](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=1) Site Installation Requirements for Steam Turbines Turbo-generator set CB 24 GT4 Order 7.318.042 This specification describes the requirements that the plant owner must meet in the area surrounding the turbine: foundation, alignment, piping, oil system, electrical installation, insulation and monitoring.

heading: 1 General
markdown: --- Page source: [page 3](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=3) 1 General The turbine supplier delivers the turbine, the gearbox, the generator and the oil system on a common base frame. The plant owner provides the foundation, the connecting piping, the cooling water supply and the electrical connections. All work must follow the drawings listed in the order documentation. Deviations require written approval by the turbine supplier. Warning: the installation area must be kept free of flammable material. Hot surfaces of the turbine casing and steam pipes reach more than 400 degrees Celsius during operation.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 3

heading: 2 Space requirements
markdown: --- Page source: [page 4](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=4) 2 Space requirements Keep a free area of at least 1.5 m around the base frame for operation and maintenance. Above the turbine, provide a crane hook height that allows the upper casing half and the rotor to be lifted out. | Component | Lifting weight (t) | Clear height above floor (m) | | --- | --- | --- | | Upper casing half | 4.2 | 5.5 | | Turbine rotor | 2.8 | 5.0 | | Generator rotor | 6.5 | 6.0 |

heading: 2.1 Access and ventilation
markdown: --- Page source: [page 5](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=5) 2.1 Access and ventilation Provide a transport route for the heaviest single part and a laydown area next to the turbine during inspections. The turbine hall must be ventilated so that the ambient temperature near the oil system stays below 45 degrees Celsius. Floor openings for piping and cables must be closed with covers that can carry the loads of maintenance work.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 5

heading: 3 Foundation design
markdown: --- Page source: [page 6](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=6) 3 Foundation design The foundation must carry the static weight of the turbo-generator set and the dynamic loads during operation, including short-circuit torque of the generator. Design the foundation as a reinforced concrete block or a table foundation on elastic supports. The natural frequencies of the foundation must stay at least 20 percent away from the running speeds of the turbine and the generator. Grout the base frame with non-shrinking grout after final alignment. 4 Alignment of turbine and driven machine The turbine, the gearbox and the generator are pre-aligned on the base frame at the factory. After the base frame is set on the foundation, check the alignment of the turbine to the driven machine at every coupling and correct it with shims. Record the alignment values in the installation report. Check the alignment again after grouting and after the connecting pipes are fitted, because pipe forces can change it.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 6

heading: 5 Piping
markdown: --- Page source: [page 7](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=7) 5 Piping Connect all pipes free of stress. Pipe forces and moments at the turbine flanges must not exceed the values in the piping drawing. 5.1 Live steam pipe Install a steam strainer and a quick-closing valve upstream of the turbine. Blow out the live steam pipe before it is connected to the turbine until no particles are found on the target plates.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 7

heading: 5.2 Exhaust steam pipe
markdown: --- Page source: [page 8](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=8) 5.2 Exhaust steam pipe The exhaust steam pipe leads to the process steam header. Provide an expansion joint and fixed points so that thermal growth does not load the turbine casing. Install a safety valve in the exhaust steam line that protects the turbine casing against excessive back pressure.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 8

heading: 5.3 Drain pipes
markdown: --- Page source: [page 9](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=9) 5.3 Drain pipes Casing drains and valve drains must slope continuously to the drain collector. Do not combine drains of different pressure levels in one pipe without check valves. Open all drains before start-up so that condensate cannot reach the turbine blading.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 9

heading: 5.4 Gland steam pipe
markdown: --- Page source: [page 10](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=10) 5.4 Gland steam pipe Leak-off steam from the shaft glands is led to a gland steam condenser or to atmosphere at a safe location. The pipe must not rise after leaving the turbine.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 10

heading: 5.5 Cooling water
markdown: --- Page source: [page 11](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=11) 5.5 Cooling water The oil cooler and the generator air cooler need cooling water at the flow rate and temperature given in the data sheet. Provide isolating valves and thermometers at the inlet and outlet of each cooler. | Consumer | Flow (m3/h) | Inlet temperature max. (C) | | --- | --- | --- | | Oil cooler | 12 | 32 | | Generator air cooler | 38 | 32 |

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 11

heading: 5.6 Blow-off line and start-up against back pressure
markdown: --- Page source: [page 12](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=12) 5.6 Blow-off line and start-up against back pressure During start-up the exhaust steam is blown off to atmosphere until the turbine is synchronized and the process header can take the steam. The required arrangement depends on the back pressure of the process header. Back pressure lower than 6 bar (g) Start up against the blow-off valve with the header valve closed. Open the header valve slowly after synchronization and close the blow-off valve at the same rate. Back pressure higher than 6 bar (g) and lower than 11 bar (g) Warm up the exhaust pipe through the bypass before start-up. Hold the back pressure with the blow-off control valve until the header pressure is reached. Back pressure higher than 11 bar (g) Start up only with the back-pressure controller in automatic mode and with the bypass open. Increase load in steps and watch the axial position of the rotor.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 12

heading: 6 Oil system
markdown: --- Page source: [page 13](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=13) 6 Oil system The oil system supplies lube oil to the bearings of turbine, gearbox and generator and control oil to the governor. Fill the system only with the oil grade given in the lubrication schedule. Flush the oil system before commissioning with the bearings bypassed until the filter stays clean for four hours.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 13

heading: 6.1 Oil tank and oil mist
markdown: --- Page source: [page 14](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=14) 6.1 Oil tank and oil mist Vent the oil tank to a safe area. The oil mist separator on the tank vent must be connected with a rising pipe and must not be blocked. Maintenance of the oil mist separator is described in the operating manual.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, Full manual page, page 14

heading: 7 Electrical installation
markdown: --- Page source: [page 15](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=15) 7 Electrical installation Connect the generator, the auxiliary motors and the control cabinet according to the circuit diagrams. Earth the base frame at two opposite corners. Run signal cables separately from power cables and use shielded cables for speed and vibration sensors.

heading: 7.1 Emergency power
markdown: --- Page source: [page 16](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=16) 7.1 Emergency power The emergency oil pump must be supplied from a battery or an emergency power supply so that the bearings are lubricated during coast-down after a power failure.

markdown: --- Page source: [page 17](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=17) 8 Insulation Insulate the turbine casing, the valves and the steam pipes after the pressure test. markdown: --- Page source: [page 18](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=18) 9 Control and monitoring The plant control system receives the turbine signals for speed, bearing temperatures, vibration, lube oil pressure and axial position. markdown: --- Page source: [page 19](/Thingworx/FileRepositories/AIDocRepository/document-knowledge/rk-t-install-spec-7318042/source/original.pdf#page=19) 9.1 Signal exchange Hard-wired signals are required for the trip commands between the turbine protection and the generator protection. ## 1 GENERAL

1 General
The turbine supplier delivers the turbine, the gearbox, the generator and the oil system on a common base frame.
The plant owner provides the foundation, the connecting piping, the cooling water supply and the electrical
connections.
All work must follow the drawings listed in the order documentation. Deviations require written approval by the
turbine supplier.
Warning: the installation area must be kept free of flammable material. Hot surfaces of the turbine casing and
steam pipes reach more than 400 degrees Celsius during operation.

heading: 2 SPACE REQUIREMENTS
markdown:
## 2 SPACE REQUIREMENTS

2 Space requirements
Keep a free area of at least 1.5 m around the base frame for operation and maintenance. Above the turbine,
provide a crane hook height that allows the upper casing half and the rotor to be lifted out.

| Component | Lifting weight (t) | Clear height above floor (m) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upper casing half | 4.2 | 5.5 |
| Turbine rotor | 2.8 | 5.0 |
| Generator rotor | 6.5 | 6.0 |

2.1 Access and ventilation
Provide a transport route for the heaviest single part and a laydown area next to the turbine during inspections. The
turbine hall must be ventilated so that the ambient temperature near the oil system stays below 45 degrees
Celsius.
Floor openings for piping and cables must be closed with covers that can carry the loads of maintenance work.

3 Foundation design
The foundation must carry the static weight of the turbo-generator set and the dynamic loads during operation,
including short-circuit torque of the generator. Design the foundation as a reinforced concrete block or a table

The natural frequencies of the foundation must stay at least 20 percent away from the running speeds of the

heading: 5.6 BLOW-OFF LINE AND START-UP AGAINST BACK PRESSURE
sectionPath: 5.6 BLOW-OFF LINE AND START-UP AGAINST BACK PRESSURE
summary: 5.6 BLOW-OFF LINE AND START-UP AGAINST BACK PRESSURE (document section).
markdown:
## 5.6 BLOW-OFF LINE AND START-UP AGAINST BACK PRESSURE

5.6 Blow-off line and start-up against back pressure
During start-up the exhaust steam is blown off to atmosphere until the turbine is synchronized and the process
header can take the steam. The required arrangement depends on the back pressure of the process header.
Back pressure lower than 6 bar (g)
Start up against the blow-off valve with the header valve closed. Open the header valve slowly after
synchronization and close the blow-off valve at the same rate.
Back pressure higher than 6 bar (g) and lower than 11 bar (g)
Warm up the exhaust pipe through the bypass before start-up. Hold the back pressure with the blow-off control
valve until the header pressure is reached.
Back pressure higher than 11 bar (g)
Start up only with the back-pressure controller in automatic mode and with the bypass open. Increase load in steps
and watch the axial position of the rotor.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 5.6 BLOW-OFF LINE AND START-UP AGAINST BACK PRESSURE, page 12

heading: 6 OIL SYSTEM
markdown:
## 6 OIL SYSTEM

6 Oil system
The oil system supplies lube oil to the bearings of turbine, gearbox and generator and control oil to the governor.
Fill the system only with the oil grade given in the lubrication schedule.
Flush the oil system before commissioning with the bearings bypassed until the filter stays clean for four hours.

6.1 Oil tank and oil mist
Vent the oil tank to a safe area. The oil mist separator on the tank vent must be connected with a rising pipe and
must not be blocked.
Maintenance of the oil mist separator is described in the operating manual.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 6 OIL SYSTEM, page 13

heading: 7 ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION
markdown:
## 7 ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION

7 Electrical installation
Connect the generator, the auxiliary motors and the control cabinet according to the circuit diagrams. Earth the
base frame at two opposite corners.
Run signal cables separately from power cables and use shielded cables for speed and vibration sensors.

7.1 Emergency power
The emergency oil pump must be supplied from a battery or an emergency power supply so that the bearings are
lubricated during coast-down after a power failure.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 7 ELECTRICAL INSTALLATION, page 15

heading: 8 INSULATION
markdown:
## 8 INSULATION

8 Insulation
Insulate the turbine casing, the valves and the steam pipes after the pressure test. Leave the flanges of the casing
joint and the instrument connections accessible.
Insulation must be protected against oil. Oil-soaked insulation is a fire hazard and must be replaced.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 8 INSULATION, page 17

heading: 9 CONTROL AND MONITORING
markdown:
## 9 CONTROL AND MONITORING

9 Control and monitoring
The plant control system receives the turbine signals for speed, bearing temperatures, vibration, lube oil pressure
and axial position. Alarm and trip values are listed in the instrument list.

9.1 Signal exchange
Hard-wired signals are required for the trip commands between the turbine protection and the generator protection.
Status and measured values may be exchanged over a fieldbus.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 9 CONTROL AND MONITORING, page 18

heading: 10 CHECKLIST BEFORE COMMISSIONING
markdown:
## 10 CHECKLIST BEFORE COMMISSIONING

10 Checklist before commissioning
- Foundation grouted and cured.
- Alignment checked after grouting and after piping.
- Live steam pipe blown out and strainer fitted.
- Oil system flushed and filled.
- Cooling water available at the required flow.
- Electrical connections tested.

10.1 Handover
The installation is handed over to the commissioning team when every item of the checklist is signed by the plant
owner and the supplier.

sourceLinks.label: RK&T install spec, 10 CHECKLIST BEFORE COMMISSIONING, page 20
